layout_structure.layout_description: This is a title slide with a clean, centered layout on a white background. At the very top, a horizontal row of four institutional logos is displayed: Technische Universität Berlin (left), Science of Intelligence (left-center), Robotics Institute Germany (center), and Penn Engineering GRASP Laboratory (right). The main title is centered in a large, black, sans-serif font. Below it, the subtitle 'CVPR 2025' appears in a smaller, blue font. The lower half of the slide contains the author list, centered in a single line with superscript numbers for affiliations. Beneath the authors, the corresponding affiliations are listed in a centered block, numbered 1 through 4. The text density is light, focusing entirely on identifying the paper, its authors, and their institutions.

layout_structure.title_text: Problem: Fails in difficult conditions, like fast movements or low light.
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a minimalist layout on a plain white background. A rectangular image is positioned in the upper-left quadrant, depicting a blue fidget spinner attached to a silver aluminum extrusion rail. Directly above the top-left corner of this image is a small label in red text that reads '30x slower'. At the bottom of the slide, there is a single, prominent line of black text that serves as the main message, stating a problem related to performance in difficult conditions. The right half of the slide is entirely empty, resulting in a very light text density and a focus on the visual example and its corresponding limitation.

The slide follows a comparison layout with two images positioned side-by-side in the top half and explanatory text in the bottom half. The top-left image shows a standard color photograph of a blue fidget spinner, with a small red caption '30x slower' placed directly above it. The top-right image displays a corresponding grayscale visualization of the same scene, likely representing event camera data, with colored tracking points (red, green, blue, and pink) overlaid on the spinner's arms. Below these figures, there are two left-aligned lines of text. The first line starts with the bold label 'Problem:' followed by a description of failure conditions like fast movements or low light. The second line starts with the bold label 'Proposed Solution:' followed by the suggested use of an event camera. The slide has a plain white background and a very light text density, focusing primarily on the visual comparison.

layout_structure.title_text: Input: Events, (query points) Output: 2D Point tracks
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a horizontal flow diagram illustrating a data processing pipeline. On the left side, under the heading 'Input: Events, (query points)', there is a 3D space-time volume plot showing a dense cloud of red and blue event points with axes labeled x, y, and t. Two specific query points, q0 and q1, are indicated with green and orange arrows. Below this plot, two callout boxes show pairs of images: a standard photograph of a fidget spinner and its corresponding event-based representation at two different time intervals. In the center of the slide, a blue hourglass-shaped icon containing the Greek letter Psi represents the transformation function or neural network. On the right side, under the heading 'Output: 2D Point tracks', a matching 3D space-time volume plot displays smooth, multi-colored trajectories representing the tracked points over time. The overall design is clean with a white background and light text density, emphasizing the visual transition from raw event data to structured point tracks.
